parsed.rationale: Sinus rhythm at about 65 bpm with Q/QS complexes and small inverted T waves in II, III and aVF, which fits an inferior infarct, but I can't see ST elevation that meets STEMI criteria (≥1 mm in two contiguous limb leads, or ≥2 mm in V2–V3) in any lead, and V2–V3 show prominent T waves with ST segments near baseline. So from this tracing alone I would not call it STEMI, even though you say the case was later confirmed as one; it may have been recorded before or after the ST elevation, or the elevation may have shown on serial ECGs.
